why: The Inspector passes on what Mrs. Straker said about the knife, which adds to her earlier account of the night.
She woke to find him dressing, and he took the knife from the dressing-table as he left the room, so the room is plainly their bedroom.
The Inspector says a disk of cork guarding the tip was found beside the body.
The dressing-table is named as where the knife had lain.

text: What was Straker's knife for? — as a weapon
why: The Inspector suggests the knife was the best weapon Straker could lay his hands on.
